source_grounding.call_chain_traced: REST POST /collections/aliases (src/actix/api/collections_api.rs:180-196 update_aliases) -> dispatcher.submit_collection_meta_op(CollectionMetaOperations::ChangeAliases) (lib/storage/src/dispatcher.rs) -> toc collection_meta_ops.rs:82-85 perform -> update_aliases (toc/collection_meta_ops.rs:299). Single sequential for-loop: per action validate-then-apply; '?' early-returns on the first failing action while actions already applied remain in alias_persistence AND on disk (each insert/remove saves immediately). Write locks held across the batch give interleaving isolation only; there is no rollback, no two-phase prepare, no test codifying partial commit (grep of tests/ for alias atomicity: zero hits; git log of the file shows no alias-atomicity intent commit).
source_grounding.note: validation_absent refers to the atomicity (all-or-nothing) mechanism the constraint requires: no transactional rollback exists anywhere in the traced chain. The per-action existence validation IS present (validate_collection_exists produces the observed 404), so the rejection side behaved as documented. by_design_in_source is rejected: the only in-source comment on this function claims the OPPOSITE ('performs several alias changes in an atomic fashion'), and no explicit maintainer annotation of intentional non-transactionality exists. sufficiency_check: grep_hit_pursued (update_aliases hit 57 files; the 4 load-bearing ones read; claim keywords actions/create_alias/alias_name all pursued to handler code).
